title: All-Policy Lower Bounds for Two-Metric Shared Assignment with a Fixed Metric Gap
banked_reason: D0.5 terminal below field: subfield score ceiling6.5<7.4, not salvageable; standalone math PASS and independent audits, aggregate panel findings unrepaired.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived and independently audited the full-policy fixed-gap square-root regret frontier, its positive-coordinate and Noarov-regular inclusion extensions, and the sharp conditional enclosure certificate; the upper algorithm is inherited and the leading minimax value remains open. D0.5 stopped below the unchanged field floor at subfield, ceiling 6.5<7.4; standalone math PASS and independent D/MAIN proof audits support the kernel, while aggregate decision-panel REVISE and all four findings remain unrepaired. There is no Lean/F certification, substrate promotion or presentation; re-raise requires materially new research or operator direction.
tldr: One shared assignment protects two fixed finite-population causal means under shuffled enrollment and assigned-vector feedback. Conditional on an expert-supplied true public slope certificate, the main frontier is \(\sqrt T/32768\le R_T(\delta)\le140\sqrt T\), uniformly for every horizon and allowed gap. The new fixed-gap all-policy converse supplies the design kernel; the full-cube prefix-IPW upper is credited to \texttt{exp\_shuffled\_twometric\_precision\_frontier}. The obstruction survives squared coordinates in \([1/64,3/4]\). A proved inclusion now transfers it to the larger finite-horizon Noarov outcome-regularity product intersected with the same public-gap class, where \(\sqrt T/131072\le R_T^{\mathrm N}(\delta)\le140\sqrt T\). This isolates a shared-propensity terminal-metric contact and makes no lower-bound claim for Noarov's scalar protocol. The conservative price \(N_T(\delta)\) has order \(T^{-3/2}\). The sharp conditional square-enclosure certification calculation is solved; scientific justification of an empirical proxy-to-counterfactual bridge and the leading minimax value remain open.
gap: Noarov, Fogliato, Bertran and Roth \cite{pmlr-v267-noarov25a}, Assumption 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, obtains fast scalar regret under a coordinate envelope, a per-row joint-energy floor, and final-horizon armwise second-moment floors. Vaze and Mishra \cite{vaze2026multiobjective}, Theorem 5, uses a population benchmark. Neither result decides the all-policy fixed-public-gap converse with shuffle depletion, an actual-table constant oracle, and a terminal maximum after expectation. The credited internal predecessor supplies the full-cube upper but its shrinking-gap converse cannot answer the fixed-gap question.
fill: The paper-owned contribution is a fixed-large-gap converse for every original-feedback randomized predictable policy and the matched flat joint frontier. Achievability retains the inherited prefix-IPW upper and proof dependency credited to \texttt{exp\_shuffled\_twometric\_precision\_frontier}. Conditional sensitivity analysis establishes that the supplied slope premise alone permits no acceleration for the conservative precision proxy. The derived functional \(N_T(\delta)=R_T(\delta)/T^2\) reports that price on the HT mean-squared-error scale. The leading-value question retains the same class, feedback, and actual-table comparator; a separate partial-identification question investigates observable certification without assuming a protocol exists.
